sources.note: Inventory only: 'Language descriptions' = the Glottolog page alone; lexical resources = Otronyi 2007 and Dancy 1966; other = Dettweiler 2003, Spencer/Yoder et al. 2014 survey, Dancy & Gray 1966, Ethnologue, LinguistList. Confirms no phonology or grammar exists in any OLAC archive.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019/2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, ed. IV. Cambridge: KWEF (index entries 'Acipa = Sagamuk', 'Busәgәmuk = Sagamuk'; entry 76 Cipu; entry 501 Zubazuba 'Source(s) McGill (2012)')
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; no 'Refs' line (no phonology, grammar or wordlist) is given for Sagamuk/Zubazuba, unlike Cinda (Mort 2012) and Cipu (McGill 2007, 2009).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Stuart McGill. 2012. The Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria. Circulation draft, May 2012. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 369 pp. (sec. 3.5.3.3 'Səgəmuk [=Zubazuba]', printed p.16)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; 'stress'/'accent' occur nowhere in 369 pp. Section 3.5.3.3 only: 'In Igwama town, three languages are spoken.. An extensive list of Zubazuba was compiled on February 2011. The speakers called their language Tusəgəmuku.' Comparative tables carry 'Eastern Acipa [?]' as empty placeholder rows; a Səgəmuk row appears only in the ethnonym table (bə-səgəmuk). No phonology of this language.

sources.citation: Otronyi, Linus (transcriber). 2007-11. Wordlist: Kamuku [cdr] - Igwama and tuRegi dialects. Nigeria Group Word List, Pilot 355 version; handwritten field sheets, 16 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 82878 (subject language Eastern Acipa [acp]).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing: scanned handwritten wordlist with no prose; Igwama (Zubazuba = Eastern Acipa per the SIL record) column has no tone or stress marks (pp.1-2 viewed as images; no scanned needed for the judgment).

sources.citation: Dettweiler, Stephen H. & Sonia G. Dettweiler. 2003 [fieldwork 1993-95]. Sociolinguistic survey (level one) of the Kamuku language cluster. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2003-003. 37 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress ('stress' absent from the text). Only phonological remark, p.6 (PDF p.6): 'Although Kamuku and Acipa are known to be tone languages, our word lists do not attempt to show tone.' Eastern Acipa wordlists (Randeggi, Bobi) in Appendix B carry no tone or stress marks; sec. 2.3 and Fig. 4 establish Eastern vs Western Acipa as distinct languages.

sources.citation: Spencer, Katharine, Carol Magnusson, Zach Yoder, Katarína Hannelová, Linus Otronyi, Yakubu Oro & Michael J. Rueck. 2014. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the 'Yara (Kamuku) people, Niger and Kaduna States, Nigeria. SIL Language & Culture Archives 60335, vi+77 pp.

sources.note: Newest survey covering the Igwama/Zubazuba (Eastern Acipa) area; may carry a note on tone/orthography in its wordlist appendix; unlikely to state stress.

sources.citation: Mort, Katharine. 2012. A Phonological Description of the Cinda [tʃìndɨ́] dialect of the Kamuku language. Draft ms., 66 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives 93650 (ch. 8 Tone, ch. 9 Stress).

sources.note: Not Eastern Acipa (describes Cinda, cind1241, the neighbouring Kamuku language) but the only Kamuku-cluster phonology with a Stress chapter; useful as a cluster-level comparandum, not as a statement for east2403. 'Not Available Online'.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2011. Tusəgəmuku (Zubazuba) wordlist, Igwama, February 2011 ('An extensive list of Zubazuba was compiled on February 2011', Blench & McGill 2012:16). Unpublished ms; possibly deposited in PARADISEC collection RB5 (Blench Nigeria recordings).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only substantial Eastern Acipa lexical record by a linguist who marks tone; if it has an introductory phonology note it would be the first statement on prosody. Not on Blench's (squatted) site per the Internet Archive's index; PARADISEC catalog returned nothing by automated download.
